To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
UV-B damage to soybean is mitigated by high PFD and UV‐A, and that the effects of UV-B on soybean are difficult to predict from experiments conducted in the laboratory.

(1) soybean plants grown in the field are more resistant to the damaging effects of UV-B radiation than are plants grown in the laboratory; (2) soybean plants in the field require a combination of reduced PFD and reduced UV-A radiation to become sensitive to UV-B radiation; (3) UV-A radiation is more effective in mitigating the effects of UV-B than is PFD.
UV-B radiation can cause significant reductions in soybean biomass production in the field, but that the sensitivity of the plant to UV-B is strongly affected by the levels of PFD and UV‐A radiation.
